name: CA_4624_4625_LogonType2_LogonProc_chrome.evtx
reason: Real content read directly: 3 successful LogonType 2 (interactive) logons via chrome.exe as the logon process, plus exactly 1 failed logon (4625) -- 4 events total. 4624/4625 are fully covered event IDs (no channel/parser gap), but this file's own signal is too thin to justify a rule: 1 failure is not a brute-force pattern (the project's own Kerberos-spray rule requires 4 distinct targets in a window, well below the real spray sample's 10, specifically to avoid firing on normal single mistypes), and nothing about the 3 successful logons is anomalous on its own. Writing a rule here would mean inventing a threshold with no real population of logon-failure samples to calibrate or benign-test it against -- exactly the overfitting this project's own discipline avoids. Not pursued this pass; revisit if a real, higher-volume failed-logon sample is ever added.

No rule exists for this pattern; writing one needs care since System connecting to \lsass/\srvsvc over SMB is also fairly common legitimate traffic -- likely needs a remote-vs-local or frequency signal to stay low-noise, not a blanket PipeName match.
